claims.text: A TextEditingController holds the current text of the field it is given; the TextField shows that text, typing changes it, and code reads it through the controller's text getter.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: TextEditingController (text getter), TextField.controller; cookbook forms/retrieve-input; SDK packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/editable_text.dart:221-261

claims.text: TextEditingController's unnamed constructor takes an optional named parameter text; the controller starts with that text, so a TextField given it opens already filled in.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: TextEditingController constructor; TextField class docs ('to set the initial value ... use a controller that already contains some text'); editable_text.dart:244

claims.text: At stage-1 _LoginScreenState has final fields _emailController/_passwordController with text 'anh.tran@example.com'/'donhang-dev-password'; _submit reads .text only on the button press; the other TextField arguments set the label and obscureText hides the password.
anh.tran@example.com is seeded customer 1 (the first row of the seed); donhang-dev-password is the one fake dev password given to all 5 seeded customers at stage-1.

Widgets inside a TextField (its EditableText; an AnimatedBuilder around its decoration) listen to the controller; when its text changes, Flutter's code for those widgets calls setState in their own State, so they rebuild. Typing stores the new text in the controller.
claims.source_hint: Flutter SDK widgets/editable_text.dart:3311, 4918-4935; material/text_field.dart:1765-1776 (AnimatedBuilder on controller); cookbook text-field-changes

claims.text: Typing into a TextField with a controller does not run the enclosing screen's build: no setState is needed and _LoginScreenState.build does not run on a keystroke (checked with a widget test on a stage-1 copy).
claims.source_hint: Flutter SDK editable_text.dart:4918-4935 (setState is in EditableTextState, not the parent); widget test in a git archive of stage-1: parent build count unchanged after enterText

claims.text: Each build of _LoginScreenState creates new TextField objects given the same controllers, so a rebuild (e.g. setState after a failed login showing the red error) keeps the typed text in the field.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: Widget (immutable configuration), State; login_screen.dart:41-57; widget test on stage-1 copy: typed email still shown after 'Exception: login failed (401)'

claims.text: TextEditingController extends ValueNotifier<TextEditingValue>, a ChangeNotifier: it keeps a list of listeners and calls each one when its value changes, so it plays the subject's role in the Observer pattern.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: TextEditingController (extends ValueNotifier), ChangeNotifier.addListener/notifyListeners; editable_text.dart:221; foundation/change_notifier.dart:139, 542

claims.text: Flutter docs: call dispose on a TextEditingController when no longer needed (the cookbook does it in the State's dispose override). ChangeNotifier.dispose, which it inherits, is for the owner to call, clears the listener list and leaves the object unusable.
claims.source_hint: refs flutter-website cookbook/forms/retrieve-input.md ('Call dispose ...'), text-field-changes.md:78-95; Flutter API docs TextEditingController, ChangeNotifier.dispose

claims.text: Flutter calls State.dispose when the State object is removed from the tree permanently.
login_screen.dart at stage-1 ends at line 67 and _LoginScreenState has no dispose method, so its two controllers are never disposed.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: git grep dispose -- DonHang.App/lib (no match); login_screen.dart:17-67

claims.text: In LoginScreen at stage-1 the only setState calls are inside _submit; none runs while the user types.
Dart's garbage collector reclaims memory of unreachable objects but never calls dispose on a controller, so whatever dispose does is skipped.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: ChangeNotifier.dispose ('should only be called by the object's owner'); dart.dev memory management / garbage collection

claims.text: If build created a new TextEditingController(text: ...) on every run and gave it to the field, a rebuild would show the starting text again and the typed text would be lost (checked with a widget test).
claims.source_hint: Flutter SDK editable_text.dart didUpdateWidget (controller swap); widget test on a stage-1 copy: field shows starting text after setState

claims.text: At stage-1 a failed sign-in (for example a wrong password) makes LoginScreen show the exception text in red above the button and stay on the screen.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: api_client.dart login (throws on non-200), login_screen.dart:34-35, 57; frontend.l1.logging-in-from-the-app Try it
